predecessors.note: The Nezak Huns (484-665), folded into alchon-huns by that dossier, which hands the Kabul valley over in 670; the Nezak page and the Turk Shahi page give 665.

successors.note: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth marched on Kabul in 870; the Saffarids held it to 878.

The Hindu Shahi dynasty (Kallar, c. 822) is this kingdom's second dynasty (the rename event of 822); after 870 it sat at Udabhandapura in Gandhara and re-conquered Kabul under Lalliya. Cliopatria ends the row in 874; the later Shahis (to 1026) need a dossier.

ledger.note: 665: Barha Tegin founds the Turk Shahi kingdom at Kabul. Infobox 665-822; 'Barha Tegin: c. 665 onward' (formal establishment 'sometime after 661 AD', from coinage); the Nezak page says the Nezaks were 'replaced by the Turk Shahis, probably first in Kabul and later throughout the territory'. The page names Kapisa and Kabul, not a boundary.

665: Arabs besiege Kabul. 'Kabul was occupied in 665 but revolted; reoccupied after a year-long siege'; 'c. 665: Barha Tegin repulsed the Arabs and retook territory as far as Arachosia and Kandahar' (Turk Shahi page); the Nezak page: ibn Samura 'occupied Kabul after a months-long siege but was soon ousted'.

666: Gandhara joins the Turk Shahis. The Turk Shahis replaced the Nezaks 'first in Zabulistan, then Kabulistan and Gandhara (666/667?)'; Tong Yabghu Qaghan's forces had occupied Gandhara 'from circa 625 AD' and the Turk Shahis 'may have been a political extension of the Yabghus of Tokharistan'. The year carries the page's question mark. [Reviewer sa-03-a: counterpart western-gokturks -> tokhara-yabghus; the western-gokturks dossier dissolves in 657, and alchon-huns gives Gandhara in 625 to the Western Turks 'establishing the Yabghus of Tokharistan'.]

673: peace with the Arabs. 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Bakra made a peace treaty acknowledging Rutbil and the King of Kabul'; the Arabs had also reached Kabul in 671 (Rabi ibn Ziyad drove Rutbil to al-Rukhkhaj). [Reviewer sa-03-a: confidence 3 -> 2; the Turk Shahi page dates Ubayd Allah's appointment to 673, not the treaty itself.]

region.text: Zabulistan and Arachosia, the Zunbils' country (Ghazni, Zamindawar, Bost)

ledger.note: 680: Rutbil's Zunbils break away. 'In 680-683, Rutbil split from his brother, the Shahi of Kabul, per al-Tabari'; the Zunbil infobox gives 'From circa 680 AD'. The Zunbils hold Zabulistan and Arachosia; Cliopatria puts their large shape in 692.
684: Arabs hold Kabul. 'Yazid ibn Ziyad was killed attacking Kabul' in 683; '684-685: Kabul briefly under Arab control' (Turk Shahi page).
685: the Arabs leave Kabul (the page gives 'briefly under Arab control' for 684-685 and no reason).

region.text: the Kabul valley and Gandhara, to which the Abbasid troops 'pushed'

ledger.note: 814: the Abbasids invade Kabul. '814/815: Abbasid troops defeated the Turk Shahis and pushed to Gandhara' (Pati Dumi, active c. 811-819); the Zunbil page has al-Ma'mun defeat 'the Kabul branch of the Turk Shahis' in 815.
816: tribute to Mecca. 'Tribute and an idol sent to Mecca (816)'; the page gives no loss of land, and Khingila had already 'submitted to al-Mahdi' c. 775-785.

822: the Brahmin vizier Kallar deposes Lagaturman and the Hindu Shahis rule Kabul. 'The dynasty was founded by Kallar in c. 822 CE after overthrowing Lagaturman, the last Turk Shahi king'; 'ruled Kabulistan, Gandhara and Punjab between 822 CE and 1026 CE'. Same kingdom and colour (rule 2); Cliopatria keeps the 'Turk Shahis' label to 874.

870: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth takes Kabul. 'In 870 CE, Ya'qub ibn al-Layth, the founder of the recently formed Saffarid dynasty marched onto Kabul'; 'The region was in Saffarid control until 878 CE before being recaptured by Lalliya'. Samanta 'lost the region of Kabul' (undated); the Zunbil page puts Yaqub's eastern campaign at 870/871.
870: the Shahis move to Udabhandapura. Infobox 'Kabul (822-870); Udabhandapura (870-1001)'; the move to Udabhanda is 'transferred there from the previous capital of Kabul'.

870: the Kabul kingdom ends; the dynasty carries on in Gandhara. Kabul goes to the Saffarids; the Shahis at Udabhandapura are the later Hindu Shahis (c. 880 Lalliya re-conquers Kabul; to 1026). Cliopatria ends the row in 874.

wars.name: Arab campaigns against Kabul
wars.outcome: Ibn Samura took Kabul in 665 and was ousted; the Turk Shahis rose in the Nezaks' place; the peace treaty of 673 acknowledged 'Rutbil and the King of Kabul'.
wars.note: 653-654 Zabul, 656 Bost and Zabulistan submit, 661 treaty brokered by the ruler of Kabul, 664-665 Kabul occupied, 671 Rabi ibn Ziyad, 673 treaty.

wars.name: Arab attack on Kabul of 683-685
wars.outcome: Yazid ibn Ziyad was killed attacking Kabul in 683; Kabul was 'briefly under Arab control' in 684-685.

wars.name: Army of Destruction and Ibn al-Ash'ath
wars.outcome: Ubayd Allah's army was defeated by the Zunbils in 698; Ibn al-Ash'ath made a peace treaty c. 700 and then rebelled. No border moved.
wars.note: The fighting was against the Zunbils (Zabulistan).

wars.name: Abbasid campaign against the Turk Shahis
wars.outcome: Abbasid troops defeated the Turk Shahis in 814/815 and pushed to Gandhara; tribute and an idol were sent to Mecca in 816; no land is said to change hands.

wars.name: Saffarid conquest of Kabul
wars.outcome: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth marched onto Kabul in 870; the Saffarids held the region to 878 until Lalliya recaptured it.
wars.note: Lalliya's recapture belongs to the Hindu Shahis dossier.

certainty.note: No treaty line is drawn on any page opened; the Hindu Kush and the Kabul valley are the only named frontier lands. The 673 treaty with the Arabs and the tribute settlements are not border lines.

notes: Five pages. The 'Kabul Shahi' page is only a disambiguation (Turk Shahis 665-850, Hindu Shahi 850-1026 there; the Turk Shahi page has 665-822, the Hindu Shahi page c. 822-1026). Cliopatria's row 561-874 is the Kabul kingdom under three dynasties: the Nezak Huns to 665 (drawn in alchon-huns, which hands the Kabul valley over in 670, five years after the 665 used here), the Turk Shahis 665-822 and the Hindu Shahis 822-870. This dossier is the Kabul Shahi state 665-870 with a rename in 822; shapes 561 and 644 are wrong (Nezak), 870 is wrong (Saffarid Kabul; the Shahis continue at Udabhandapura). Needs: a hindu-shahis dossier from 870 (Udabhandapura, Lalliya's 878 recapture, Punjab, 1026) whose colour should continue this one's; zunbils (written here). Tokharistan (Bactria and Badakhshan) is taken out of every shape (page: Yabghu suzerainty): the Yabghus/Tokharistan have no dossier in this batch (Western Gokturks to 660, then Tang/Arabs). The Turk Shahis were 'nominal Tang protectorate since circa 658 AD' (Jibin governors under Anxi, 661; Tang titles 719/720 and 745) and tributary to the Abbasids from al-Mahdi (c. 775-785): these suzerainties are recorded by the Tang and Abbasid dossiers, not here. No rulers list: the page dates only some reigns (Barha Tegin c. 665, Tegin Shah c. 680-739, Fromo Kesaro 739-745, Bo Fuzhun from 745, Khingila c. 775-785, Pati Dumi c. 811-819, Lagaturman to c. 822). Gazetteer: Udabhandapura and Kapisa are not places; Kabul is. The 673 date is the treaty, though the Zunbil page puts it at the Zunbils' recognition; Kabul's 671 attack is in the ledger note only.
